edits.text: Keep a preposition, an opening parenthesis, or a numeral together with the word or phrase that completes its object or unit — the object noun, measurement unit, or the closing parenthesis.

Keep a preposition, an opening parenthesis, or a numeral together with the immediately following word or phrase that completes its object or unit. Concretely: keep prepositions with their object noun/NP (e.g. "of the city"), numerals with their measurement unit (e.g. "105 miles"), and "(" with the text up to and including its matching ")".

- Would a cut separate a preposition, an opening parenthesis, a numeral, or an internal noun modifier (e.g., an "of"-phrase) from the word or phrase that completes its object, measurement unit, or the closing parenthesis? Such splits leave incomplete expressions and often cause mistranslation or contradiction.
